items.title: 구찌, 밀란 패션위크서 '더 스토어 쇼' 공개... 박규영·황인엽 참석
items.summary: FashionSeoul reports on Gucci's 'The Store Show' presented by creative director Demna at Milan Fashion Week, staged as a mock retail environment split into zones for archetypes like 'the Rebellious Aristocrat' and 'the Snob.' Korean stars Park Gyu-young and Hwang In-yeop attended alongside Cardi B, Romeo Beckham, Edward Norton and Shawn Mendes; the show streamed globally on Gucci's platforms.

items.title: 140만원짜리 구찌 신발에 붙은 '메이드인 차이나'... '중국산 명품' 통할까
items.summary: Financial News details Korean retail pricing for Gucci's new 'Made in China' Drip sneakers: a canvas model at 1.6 million won and a nylon model at 1.42 million won, versus roughly $1,000 in the US and 800 euros in Europe. It cites a Berenberg analyst noting tension between the China provenance and the luxury positioning Gucci is trying to reclaim, despite the brand's insistence Italy stays central.

items.title: "수백만원짜리 가방 가죽 갈라졌는데, 환불 안 해준대요"... 명품 브랜드 피해구제 신청 잇따라
items.summary: Segye Ilbo reports that Korea's consumer agency logged 674 damage-relief filings against 13 major luxury brands (including Gucci) from 2021 through August 2026, with quality defects accounting for 77.2% of disputes and 50 filings specifically seeking purchase cancellation/refunds; the piece frames recurring refusal to refund damaged leather goods as a sector-wide consumer-protection issue.

items.title: "할머니 집 같아" 탄식...구찌 매장 '폐쇄 선언' 초유의 사태
items.summary: Hankyung's piece on Kering's 'ReconKering' restructuring (announced April 16) reports Gucci will shut roughly 125 stores by 2030, with CEO Luca De Meo saying some stores 'look like a grandmother's house' and conceding China was once an easy growth market for Gucci; included here as background context recirculating amid this week's store-exit and quality-complaint coverage in Korea (NOTE: older than the 14-day freshness window but provided as the only direct source locatable for the still-circulating 'closure declaration' quote; treat as background, not a fresh signal).

items.title: 싱글벙글 명품 브랜드 구찌 근황
items.summary: Popular DCInside 'real-time best' board post (29 screenshots from an SBS News segment) summarizing Gucci's sales roughly halving over recent years and the new Made-in-China sneaker labels; comment thread treats the brand's struggles as symptomatic of broader luxury-sector trouble rather than Gucci-specific.

items.title: Gucci为何打破多年传统选择在中国生产运动鞋？
items.summary: Weibo fashion-account explainer thread on why Gucci broke its 'Made in Italy' tradition for the Drip/slip-on sneakers, summarizing the brand's stated rationale (technical capability, not cost-cutting) alongside skeptical reader comments questioning whether provenance now matters less than price for China-made luxury goods.

items.title: 消费者对Gucci中国制造鞋的接受度如何
items.summary: Weibo Q&A-style community thread polling consumer acceptance of the China-made Gucci sneakers; discussion splits between users who say origin no longer matters if quality holds and others who say a nameplate luxury brand should not outsource manufacturing visibly, echoing the broader backlash narrative in press coverage.

items.title: "重现"经典，看到了GUCCI的更多可能
items.summary: Netease fashion piece aggregating Xiaohongshu sentiment on Gucci, noting the platform hosts 500,000+ user notes on the brand but that recent Gen Z commentary increasingly calls the designs 'boring' and jokes they 'won't buy Gucci unless it's discounted,' with one widely-quoted comment comparing a Gucci purchase unfavorably to spending the same money on a trip.

items.title: 구찌, 2026 봄·여름 아이웨어 캠페인 공개
items.summary: Esquire Korea covers Gucci's Spring/Summer 2026 eyewear campaign, featuring oversized square frames and retro cat-eye silhouettes with signature bamboo and Double-G hardware; included for context on the brand's ongoing accessory-category marketing push, though dated outside the fresh window and should be weighted accordingly.

items.title: グッチは業績の立て直しに向けて動き出したのか？
items.summary: FashionNetwork Japan analysis of Gucci's H1 2026 results (sales down 9% reported / 5% comparable to 2.757 billion euros) under CEO Luca De Meo's 'Riconquering' turnaround plan, covering the three-collection creative roadmap (La Famiglia, Primavera, Cruise), the new 'Gucci Racing' platform entering Formula 1, and regional performance showing Asia-Pacific excluding Japan down 5% versus North America up 9%; older context piece retained for the APAC performance detail relevant to NEA.
